content: It implies withdrawal from some things in order to deal effectively with others.
author: William James
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. We are conditioned to believe that more is always better—more possessions, more accomplishments, more stimulation. Yet our accumulation usually brings more anxiety, maintenance, and mental clutter.

Across his life and work, William James saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Wealth is not having endless things; it is wanting very little. When you realize that your deepest needs for peace, connection, and purpose cannot be bought, you become truly unshakeable.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
